reservoir_ep05_001.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_001.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-one, Yue read her mother's letter again over breakfast and spilled a little tea beside the page. She lifted the envelope before the wet edge reached it. Her mother would have called that an adequate explanation of why papers should not be put under cups. Yue smiled at the imagined sentence because it sounded like a person, not a lesson she had invented to comfort herself. The actual letter remained dry. Outside, the grain house's morning workers were laughing at Tian's basket, which had acquired another unnecessary knot.

reservoir_ep05_002.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_002.text: The letter proposed days in a later warm-season interval when a visit would be welcome. Her mother did not ask Yue to abandon the next morning's paid task. She wanted an honest answer about what the daughter could actually do. The household had its own work, care arrangements and preferences to compare. Yue placed those offered days beside the grain term's real end, then left a separate blank for any future study she might accept. No funded new instruction existed yet, and no hopeful invitation should be treated as a booked appointment.

reservoir_ep05_003.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_003.text: Her mother described the smaller household tasks she chose to keep doing and the heavier ones she left to actual help. She disliked being told that accepting help meant she had given up. The old shoulder limits remained; the years lost to the earlier cost had not returned. She had nonetheless decided which shelf to clear, which tea to refuse and which neighbor's joke deserved an answer. Yue read the ordinary details slowly. They prevented her private fear from turning a whole living person into a problem awaiting the daughter's next cultivation stage.

reservoir_ep05_004.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_004.text: Fu joined the table carrying a bowl and asked whether the reply had finally come. Yue offered the tea complaint, not the private care page. Fu laughed and said every household had someone who believed a bitter cup proved virtue. She then grew serious enough to ask what kind of visit Yue wanted. Yue answered too quickly: a useful one. Fu asked useful to whom. The question remained after the bowls were empty. Yue wanted to help, to listen, to see her mother and perhaps to stop feeling guilty; those wishes did not all mean the same thing.

reservoir_ep05_005.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_005.text: At the public veranda, Qiu was watching the appointed keeper read the morning mark. Yue waited until the task finished before asking about the visitor house's later correspondence route. Qiu supplied the actual receiving contact beyond the grain term and said it would need updating if Yue moved. She did not ask to read the family letter. Yue appreciated the small ordinary respect. The steward could help make a route function without becoming the authority who decided whether a daughter ought to visit or whether a mother's letter sounded urgent.

reservoir_ep05_006.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_006.text: The water below them carried an thin sheet of ice at its shaded edge. It was not thick enough to bear any accepted load. Qiu set the public barrier and turned back toward the office. Yue stayed at the sound viewing place and watched the sheet break quietly when the feeder stirred. She thought about how often she had pictured other people's lives as something that could be repaired from a distance. Her mother had sent a page full of choices. A visit should begin by hearing those choices in person, rather than arriving with a brilliant answer already prepared.

reservoir_ep05_007.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_007.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-two, Yue completed her eighth accepted grain day. Zhou assigned the corrected current-stock summary and one ordinary receiving comparison. The half-unit damaged fraction remained rejected, and the changed dates stayed visible. Tian had started making his copies slightly less ornamental so the important marks were easier to see. He asked whether this meant he was becoming dull. Yue said the basket made that unlikely. He pretended to be wounded, then produced a page whose clean distinction between nominal sacks and usable grain would have pleased any practical reader.

reservoir_ep05_008.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_008.text: Zhou paid the day's three copper, bringing Yue's actual grain wages to twenty-four. She counted them without assigning a future purpose before checking the private family question. Grain money could support her own real visit or an accepted care expense later, but a remittance would need an actual receiver and a purpose her mother agreed to. The wage receipt itself carried no family decision. She put the cash in the ordinary purse and let the letter's offered days remain a comparison, rather than announcing a promise she had not yet priced or booked.

reservoir_ep05_009.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_009.text: That evening, Jing showed Yue the apron mend they had made together. Its thread had held through an awkward cupboard catch, which Jing had now moved under her ordinary maintenance order. The custodian grinned and called the cloth the only reservoir improvement they had jointly certified. Yue said its balance after interrupted sleep remained unmeasured. They both laughed, then Jing put the apron down and asked how home sounded. Yue said it sounded like her mother. The answer was less informative than a medical summary and more satisfying to say aloud.

reservoir_ep05_010.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_010.text: Jing's father had once told her that a child who visited only to inspect was not much better company than a clerk sent to tax the beans. She offered the memory without applying it as a verdict on Yue. Her father wanted ordinary company and could refuse practical help he had not requested. Yue asked whether Jing found that difficult. She said yes, especially when she knew how to make something work. The skill was real; knowing when another person wished to use it was a different part of the relationship.

reservoir_ep05_011.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_011.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-three, Tian carried the water trial's public record to its next review shelf. He kept the selected mechanism and actual cost visible, rather than writing a single sentence that made every household happier forever. Fu checked the part about her own household before it was filed. Yue stood nearby as the trial's agreed observer. The current outcome could now affect the next proposal and the available fund. It would not be turned into a statistic on her cultivation page, where none of its real household consequences would be visible.

reservoir_ep05_012.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_012.text: The household receiver asked how the selected trial should shape the coming market interval. An unchanged quantity could still be obtained through different hours or handling, and the two plans had used different resources. Fu wanted the actual completed result discussed before a fresh offer was made. Qiu opened the signed source rather than relying on somebody's cheerful memory of the review. Yue could hear Tian getting ready to tell the basket joke again. She touched his sleeve, and he saved it for supper. This question needed the water account first.

reservoir_ep05_013.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_013.text: The turn exchange had left six copper unspent. At the next review, the members ratified its use for the west water-shelter's two worn door catches: three for accepted ordinary materials and three for one worker-day of fitted repair. The changed household mornings remained a separate bounded agreement, with sleep and work checked before any extension. Fu could continue the agreed collection without another neighbor's free fetching. Yue saw the preserved money become actual infrastructure, rather than remaining an abstract claim that the cheaper plan had won.

reservoir_ep05_014.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_014.text: The buffer trial had spent the six-copper remainder, so the west water-shelter's door-catch replacement had no funded order yet. Qiu kept its windy use restricted under the current inspection and offered the sound existing waiting place. Fu wanted two more later receipts during actual grain collisions. She chose to pay one handling equivalent, three copper, from wages her own grain work had already paid. The qualified worker accepted the two specified intervals. Nobody assigned the cost to Yue, an unwilling neighbor or a public fund already exhausted.

reservoir_ep05_015.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_015.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-four, Yue completed her ninth accepted grain day and received three copper, bringing completed wages to twenty-seven. Tian had misplaced a public blank form under his mending, then found it before copying any current account. He held it up as if it had returned from the mountains. Zhou asked whether the mountains had signed the receiving mark. The joke followed Yue through the afternoon's ordinary comparison and made her less tempted to turn every small mistake into evidence of a person's deeper failure.

reservoir_ep05_016.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_016.text: At the meal table, Fu asked whether Yue would write her mother about the reservoir. Yue said yes, but wondered how much to include. Fu suggested beginning with something the mother would want to picture. Yue thought of the grain-house basket, the color of the weed between stones and the wind striking the shutters. A complete institutional account would fit badly inside a private letter. Her mother had asked about her daughter's hat. Perhaps an honest description of what living here felt like could answer more than a list of carefully successful tasks.

reservoir_ep05_017.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_017.text: She began that evening with the basket's ridiculous voyage and admitted that Tian's third telling had almost sent it into the high basin. She labeled the joke naturally, trusting her mother's ability to recognize it. Then she described the ordinary cold, the sound visitor path and the small paid grain work. The page took longer than she expected because she wanted to sound useful before she sounded happy. When she noticed the order, she crossed out a solemn opening sentence and left the basket first.

reservoir_ep05_018.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_018.text: Jing found her smiling over the revision. Yue offered the joke aloud, and Jing said her father would prefer the basket to another respectful paragraph about his health. She had learned to ask him about the garden before the shoulder, while still remembering which lifting tasks remained restricted. Yue asked whether that felt evasive. Jing said the shoulder was part of him, but he had planted beans too. The distinction gave Yue something practical to try without allowing her to ignore the care details that actually needed an answer.

reservoir_ep05_019.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_019.text: Her mother's reply had described the chosen ordinary shoulder review on Day One Thousand Twenty-two. She had attended it through the local arrangement she herself funded, and its instructions preserved the existing limits and shorter kiln tasks. Qiu Fang remained her chosen paid local helper for two afternoons each month, supported by her own work and household budget. The city's optional support decision had closed; any selected block was delivered and reported. Yue read those facts as a living arrangement to respect, rather than a debt she had authority to replace.

reservoir_ep05_020.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_020.text: The appointment had not returned the lost years. Her mother said the clinician had helped her distinguish a tolerable small task from a heavier one that still left pain. She was annoyed that the household shelf remained too high and delighted that Qiu Fang had told the neighbor not to improve her tea without asking. Yue laughed again. Ordinary care had made particular hours more manageable. It had not delivered the impossible restoration her daughter might secretly hope a future stage would provide.

reservoir_ep05_021.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_021.text: Yue asked in the draft whether a lower shelf would be welcome during a later visit. She did not promise to arrive and remake the house. Her mother might prefer a different place or have an accepted carpenter already arranged. The question felt smaller than Yue's desire to help, which was precisely why it could be answered honestly. She would also ask whether the offered visiting days remained suitable after the next kiln schedule. A family comparison needed each person's real calendar, not the daughter's picture of an always-waiting home.

reservoir_ep05_022.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_022.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-five, she walked the public garden with Fu during an agreed free interval. Fu's brother had repaired the boot knot once more after realizing it caught on the carrying frame. She showed Yue the new flat tie and said he had finally learned that strength was not the same as bulk. Yue wanted to send that sentence home, then decided the useful story belonged to Fu unless she agreed. Fu readily offered the harmless knot tale. She kept the private work-sheet details for her household.

reservoir_ep05_023.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_023.text: A small ordinary bird landed on the garden wall and stole a loose seed from the swept edge. Fu watched it leave, then asked whether the basin's empty-sky name made Yue expect something remarkable. Yue admitted it had. She had imagined still water and a quiet mind becoming the same achievement. Fu pointed at the moving feeder and the grain dust on her own sleeve. The basin was beautiful, she said, and people still had to finish lunch before the next shift. Yue found herself liking the actual place more than the imagined one.

reservoir_ep05_024.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_024.text: At the garden's end, Fu asked a sharper question. Was Yue postponing every visit until she could bring home proof of improvement? Yue stopped walking. She had not written that idea in any agreement, but parts of it had guided her for a long time. She wanted to answer that the next stage would make her work more dependable, which was true within tested conditions and did not answer the family question. Fu waited without supplying a verdict. Yue finally said she did not want her mother to see another unfinished attempt.

reservoir_ep05_025.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_025.text: Fu asked whether her mother had demanded a completed daughter. Yue laughed painfully at the phrase. The letter had asked about a hat and a date she could actually keep. It had named real limitations and then moved on to a complaint about tea. The mother had not treated herself as an unfinished task either. Yue sat on the accepted garden bench and let that recognition be uncomfortable. She could pursue the reservoir examination and still decide what kind of company she wished to be before a certificate existed.

reservoir_ep05_026.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_026.text: The public review's next interval concerned the selected water plan's consequences. Qiu had its actual source record open: either the remaining six had been ratified for door repair, or the fund had already been spent on the buffer and Fu had accepted a new private handling cost. The west shelter's current use would differ accordingly. Yue returned from the garden in time for the comparison she had agreed to observe. Private family questions could change how she heard that public choice without allowing her to replace its facts with a lesson about herself.

reservoir_ep05_027.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_027.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-six, the qualified worker fitted the two catches and checked the door against the present wind. Qiu accepted the current shelter under the repaired ordinary conditions. The short icy step still had its own closure; visitors used the sound longer route. Liu's partner was pleased to have a quieter waiting place and reminded him that their next household review still mattered. Repairing a public door did not repay her lost sleep automatically. The selected plan had changed both ordinary access and the next use of a finite fund.

reservoir_ep05_028.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_028.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-six, the cooperative confirmed finite reuse of the checked jars and tray through Day One Thousand Sixty, with return at the next receiver. Jing verified their condition before the second private handling interval. Fu would report received water and any measured loss, rather than expecting the purchased labor to guarantee a perfect twenty litres. The household had gained a later receiving possibility by choosing a continued expense. Yue helped label the source of this new payment separately from the completed public trial, so one could not be billed again as the other.

reservoir_ep05_029.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_029.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-seven, the meal-house cook announced that Zhou's birthday would be marked with a pot of ordinary sweet soup after the current work ended. Zhou protested that nobody knew his exact birthday. The cook said his own account had supplied the date three years ago when he wanted an extra peach. Tian seized on this evidence with such pleasure that Zhou regretted teaching him careful source comparison. Yue offered to help wash bowls during the agreed free interval, and the evening acquired a purpose entirely separate from the grain ledger.

reservoir_ep05_030.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_030.text: The soup contained dried fruit from the cook's private gift store. Each person took a small bowl, and Zhou received the one with the chipped blue rim he always chose. Qiu arrived after her round and brought an ordinary sprig of early blossom from her own garden. Jing wore the repaired apron because she had been caught helping with the stove. Yue could still see the little uneven stitch they had made together. The room looked warmer than its shutters could explain, full of people who had stopped asking a useful evening to prove anything.

reservoir_ep05_031.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_031.text: Tian announced that Zhou was old enough to have personally invented grain. Zhou told him the invention had been easy compared with persuading Tian to return a copied form to its proper shelf. Liu sent bread with a message calling every guest a terrible judge of birthdays but a promising consumer of supper. Fu laughed until soup nearly spilled onto her sleeve. Yue looked around the table and wanted her mother to hear its noise. She would describe the chipped bowl and the cook's exact argument, rather than reducing the evening to a report that she was doing well.

reservoir_ep05_032.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_032.text: After the first bowls, the failed-comparison worker sang a short tune she had learned while waiting at another institution. Her voice caught on one high note, and she made a cheerful face before taking a lower line. Tian drummed softly on his repaired basket until the cook threatened to serve it soup. Yue listened with her ordinary hands folded on the table. The singer's uncompleted examination had not suspended her ability to make a room happy. Her actual paid accounting work and recovered health would have their own next decisions later.

reservoir_ep05_033.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_033.text: Jing asked Yue to sing the tune from her home kiln. She remembered only the opening and warned them before beginning. Fu took the missing line in a different version, and they argued about the final word while everyone else enjoyed the disagreement. Yue's version smelled in memory of warm clay and an ordinary floor washed after work. Her mother's face entered that memory at a younger age. The present letter still belonged to the older woman at home. Both could matter without requiring one to replace the other.

reservoir_ep05_034.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_034.text: When the room grew quiet, Zhou said he had once planned to leave grain work for a more impressive profession. He had kept postponing the road until another person needed a receiving clerk, then found that he liked making a store understandable enough for people to use it without him. Yue asked whether he regretted the untraveled road. He said sometimes, especially when travelers brought better jokes than his own. The answer's incompleteness pleased her. A life could be chosen and still contain an honest loss.

reservoir_ep05_035.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_035.text: Qiu stayed behind to stack the washed bowls with Yue. She said the cook had offered the celebration, not demanded a public confession from everybody growing older. Yue laughed and admitted she had nearly turned Zhou's answer into a lesson for her letter. Qiu handed her the chipped blue bowl. Some things deserved to travel as stories first. If the mother wanted to ask about the grain receiver's life, she could. The visitor did not have to arrive at every private conversation with its meaning already polished.

reservoir_ep05_036.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_036.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-eight, Yue completed her tenth accepted grain day. Zhou had evidently survived the soup and resumed his practical temper. He assigned the ordinary storage-date comparison, while Tian handled current public dispatch copies. Yue found a misaligned column rather than a missing sack and corrected the copy against its retained original. The work ended at the posted hour. Its three-copper wage brought her completed total to thirty, with six accepted days remaining in the finite term. She felt tired enough to enjoy stopping.

reservoir_ep05_037.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_037.text: A private family draft lay waiting in her room, now much less solemn. She wrote that Zhou sometimes regretted roads he had not taken, then crossed out his name because her mother did not need a new acquaintance introduced through a stranger's private admission. She kept the birthday joke. A letter could show her actual company without transferring every offered confidence. The page gained the singer's crooked high note and the chipped bowl. Yue found that describing joy made the distance feel sharper and more bearable at the same time.

reservoir_ep05_038.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_038.text: She added the care questions plainly. Had the proposed lower shelf already been arranged, would a later visit still fit the kiln's shorter tasks, and which ordinary days would her mother prefer? Qiu Fang's two chosen afternoons each month remained funded from the mother's own household budget. Yue offered no new helper block as if she could order it into existence. If her mother wanted a separately priced extra service, they could discuss its real source later. Today the daughter wanted to hear what would actually make a visit welcome.

reservoir_ep05_039.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_039.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty-nine, the family forwarding receiver sent a notice correcting one place name on a future route. Yue read it against the address already used successfully and updated the draft envelope. The actual letter would leave through the next accepted private dispatch. Tian offered to decorate its edge with a basket, then remembered that a receiver needed room for the stamp. He drew a tiny one on a separate scrap instead. Yue laughed and put the scrap inside with the ordinary jokes she had chosen to send.

reservoir_ep05_040.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_040.text: Fu joined her on the public garden bench while the afternoon grain shift continued elsewhere. She said she was glad Yue had written about the soup. Her own brother once sent a whole page about work and forgot to say whether he still liked the place. Yue admitted that she sometimes treated liking a place as evidence she was betraying home. Fu considered this, then said a person could miss one table while enjoying another. The hard part was deciding when to leave a real opportunity for a real visit.

reservoir_ep05_041.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_041.text: The two women watched Tian cross the yard with the basket. He was carrying only forms and held it with exaggerated care. Fu asked whether the basket might become their institution's official emblem. Yue said it would probably resign after reading the duties. They laughed, and the sound made a nearby ordinary bird leave the wall in indignation. The bird had its own excellent reasons to avoid noisy people. For a few minutes, Yue's homecoming question rested beside them without needing to be answered by every event she saw.

reservoir_ep05_042.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_042.text: Qiu's next public review would close the selected trial's immediate aftermath. The actual water record now included either the paid catch repair after the exchange or the finite additional private buffer service after the spent public fund. Future household planning would use that result and the current source conditions. Yue would return the last permitted observation counterpart and let the named receiver keep the continuing task. The family letter could be ready the same evening. She liked the thought of finishing one small agreed thing before promising another.

reservoir_ep05_043.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_043.text: Yue recorded the actual six-copper repair and the continuing roster's review date. Fu chose to mention the repaired shelter in an offered public account, while keeping her brother's private work sheet at home. Tian admired the new catches with the gravity he usually reserved for his basket. He asked whether the door would acquire a heroic name. Qiu said she would settle for Quiet Enough To Hear The Gauge. The joke made Fu laugh, and the shelter's practical soundness remained more useful than whatever name they gave it.

reservoir_ep05_044.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_044.text: At the review, Fu put the private three-copper receipt beside the completed public handling record. She said later collection had let her keep paid work and share an evening meal, but she wanted a less expensive longer-term arrangement. Qiu accepted that next question without promising new money. Tian carried the returned empty tray by the sound route under his own accepted task and refused to let it join the basket's legendary fleet. The chosen buffer had produced real evenings and a real household cost; the restricted west shelter remained unfinished work.

reservoir_ep05_045.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_045.text: On Day One Thousand Sixty, the public receiver accepted the selected water trial's last immediate counterpart. Fu kept her household original, the cooperative kept its own property record, and Yue's agreed observation was complete. The result would shape the next household question without making the visitor its permanent owner. Tian tied the public packet neatly, then stopped himself from improving the knot after it was already sound. Yue told him Fu's brother would appreciate the restraint. He said he would send the brother a drawing rather than an instruction.

reservoir_ep05_046.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_046.text: Fu asked Yue to walk with her to the sound evening waiting place. The basin's reflected sky had gone copper near the far ridge, while the outgoing channel still moved through its measured turn. Fu said she sometimes felt guilty enjoying a quiet evening after using money on a practical problem. Someone else always had a different need. Yue understood the feeling. The finite fund had required a real choice; the choice's cost belonged in its record. It did not require them to refuse every ordinary pleasure until every need in the watershed was gone.

reservoir_ep05_047.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_047.text: At the bench, Fu described the first supper she had shared with her brother after a collision-free weighing day. He had burned the onions and insisted the new boot tie was proof that he could cook precisely. She told the story with affection sharp enough to make Yue laugh. The supper had happened under the actual selected arrangement, with its altered routines or handling costs still real. A consequence could be a paid interval preserved, a household margin spent, and two people sitting down together despite bad onions.

reservoir_ep05_048.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_048.text: Yue wanted her own visit to contain that kind of ordinary hour. She had pictured arriving with some hard-won practical improvement, but now imagined hearing her mother complain about a shelf and deciding together whether to move it. There would be work she missed on the plateau. Someone else might receive an opportunity while she traveled. She could not make the cost vanish by naming the visit virtuous. The question was whether she was willing to accept it for a conversation her mother actually wanted, rather than promising both complete availability and perfect professional timing.

reservoir_ep05_049.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_049.text: Fu said she would not answer that question for her. She could help compare the days once the actual offers existed. Yue was grateful for the refusal's warmth. It left her with a decision instead of a judgment. They walked back as Tian crossed the yard carrying his now-famous basket perfectly level. He called that the result of long recovered trials. Fu told him not to claim a new realm without checking tomorrow's ordinary wrists. Yue laughed at the joke, whose small familiarity made it feel less lonely to wait for a larger answer.

reservoir_ep05_050.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_050.text: That night, she finished the private reply. She described the soup, the weed, the basket and the useful small work, then answered her mother's offered visiting interval with a conditional question. Could they keep those days under consideration while Yue compared whatever funded study and ordinary employment were actually offered? She would not ask the family to wait indefinitely or keep every day free. Her mother could change her mind. The letter's care questions remained clear and modest, and its ordinary jokes sounded like a daughter who had finally remembered to be present on the page.

reservoir_ep05_051.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_051.text: On Day One Thousand Sixty-one, Yue completed her eleventh accepted grain day. The receiver's current comparison used the same physical stock sources and updated actual dispatch dates. Tian worked beside her without trying to turn speed into proof that he had mastered the whole job. At the noon interval he showed her a correctly labeled old canceled form, preserved for a comparison rather than revived as current instruction. Yue said she would have been tempted to throw it away when she was younger. He said his own embarrassing forms were becoming a substantial historical collection.

reservoir_ep05_052.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_052.text: Zhou checked the finished work and paid three copper. Across eleven accepted equivalents Yue had now earned thirty-three, leaving five specifically scheduled grain days within the finite term. The lodge and meal receivers retained their own actual provision records. Yue would need to finish those five days before the current commission closed. She had space for a private dispatch today and had not concealed it inside a paid grain hour. The letter mattered enough to deserve its own time, source and actual receiving handover.

reservoir_ep05_053.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_053.text: At the private desk, she paid one copper from completed personal wages and gave the letter to the accepted courier receiver. The envelope's corrected place name matched the current route. Its stamp recorded actual departure on Day One Thousand Sixty-one. Yue's earlier plateau letter had already met the city's latest promised sending date; this new reply kept that ordinary connection active without creating a compulsory reply deadline for her mother. She retained the fee receipt and the sender's counterpart, then watched the courier put the envelope among its real outgoing companions.

reservoir_ep05_054.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_054.text: Tian's tiny basket drawing went inside, with a sentence naming its joke. Yue had decided against enclosing a copied institutional water chart. Her mother had asked about the place and the daughter, not requested the role of outside reviewer for a local household dispute. She could describe the evenings the selected work had helped make possible in ordinary words. The actual public source would remain at its proper shelf. She liked imagining the small drawing reaching the familiar table where her mother would decide whether its basket resembled any sensible object.

reservoir_ep05_055.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_055.text: The paid dispatch left Yue with thirty-two of the grain wages, apart from the actual personal travel remainder. She did not treat the authorized last fifteen wages as cash already received. If she later chose a visit or study fee, she would compare real available money and the actual offer. The arithmetic was simple enough that it did not need to become the letter's main subject. It gave her a truthful foundation from which to promise a particular journey when the date came, rather than a wish she could only sustain by borrowing somebody else's fund.

reservoir_ep05_056.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_056.text: Jing found her at the public veranda after dispatch. Yue said she had finally sent a reply she liked. Jing asked whether it included the basket. It did. The custodian nodded as if this were the most important correct result in the room. Then she showed Yue a loose button from her own coat, purchased with an ordinary blue thread that matched badly. Yue offered to help sew it during their next free interval. Neither woman pretended the helpful little task had to lead toward instruction, examination or a permanent exchange of favors.

reservoir_ep05_057.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_057.text: Qiu's next term review would concern the remaining winter-city access, source returns and actual closing reports. She brought the public schedule to the meal house and asked Yue to compare it with the five outstanding grain dates. They fitted. The local receiving agent had been designated to close the bounded city access by Day One Thousand Seventy-four, so a far-road courier acknowledgment would not silently prolong it. New instruction, if offered later, would start only after that closure and a different accepted fund. Yue put the final dates where she could find them tomorrow.

reservoir_ep05_058.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_058.text: Fu read the public schedule and offered to attend the part concerning her own permitted household account. She would keep the private calendar at home and answer only the question she agreed to hear. Liu sent another bread message, this one declaring that public debates should never be booked while crust was at its best. Tian copied the receiving hour accurately despite finding the message funnier than the schedule. The room now held several actual plans that could coexist without requiring one person's endless availability. Yue enjoyed seeing the arrangement take that practical shape.

reservoir_ep05_059.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_059.text: The failed-comparison worker returned from her accepted ordinary accounting interval with a little potted flower bought from personal wages. She placed it on the visitor-room sill and invited anyone interested to look. Yue admired the uneven red petals and asked whether the plant liked the cold room. The woman said she was still learning and would follow the gardener's ordinary advice rather than make the flower prove a cultivation metaphor. They sat near it for a while, talking about soup. An unpassed examination had left room for something new that belonged to its buyer.

reservoir_ep05_060.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_060.text: As the sky darkened, Yue thought about the possible reservoir study. She wanted the balance for the actual bounded tasks it might help her perform, and because learning had become a part of her own chosen life. She also wanted to visit home before turning every family encounter into evidence of whether the learning had been worthwhile. Those desires could come into conflict. She would need to choose when real offers arrived. For now, the letter had left, the grain day was paid, and the mother remained a person who could answer or change her visiting preference.

reservoir_ep05_061.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_061.text: At the bottom of the pack, Yue found a small cloth patch she had carried longer than the present coat. Its old blue thread crossed a newer brown repair. She had once wanted to replace every uneven stitch when she learned to work more neatly. Her mother had said the cloth was still sound and the colors made it easier to find. Yue spread it on the bed and smiled at the practical argument. Something could retain its history without becoming too damaged to use.

reservoir_ep05_062.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_062.text: Tian knocked at the open public stair and called goodnight from below. He wanted to know whether Yue's mother would understand the basket drawing. Yue said she might criticize its rather precarious carrying angle. He asked her to report the criticism faithfully. The thought made Yue laugh, because it gave the next family reply a small ordinary question waiting at this table too. She folded the cloth patch into her private belongings, then answered that she would send whichever comment her mother actually chose to offer.

reservoir_ep05_063.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_063.text: The house quieted in stages. Zhou went back to his local rooms, Fu left for her accepted return passage, and Qiu began the named watch with its current receiver. Tian checked that the basket was dry before storing the last blank forms. Jing put her owned mending needle away. Yue climbed to the paid visitor room with no institutional instrument in her pack and no public packet left on her private bed. The open space where the family letter had been looked less like absence now. It looked like a message actually traveling.

reservoir_ep05_064.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep05_064.text: Before sleeping, she remembered her mother joking about the hat. Yue found it on the peg, still patched, and inspected the ordinary tie that had kept it from the plateau wind. It was adequate. She imagined wearing it through the familiar home doorway on some agreed later day, then let the picture remain unfinished. A seventh-stage practitioner could hope without making the imagined future a result. Tonight she could sleep under the grain term's real roof and wake for the remaining work, with a better letter already on its way.
